title: [Livestream 7/12/2024] Immigration from and emigration to a European country in 2009
prompt: The pie charts show people’s reasons for immigration to a European country in 2009 and reasons for emigration from a European country in 2009. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The pie charts give information about the proportions of migrants entering and leaving a European country in 2009 for various reasons.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, it can be seen that the most common reason for immigrants going to this country was to accompany their family members, while emigrants left it to pursue offers of employment abroad.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding job- and study-related purposes, 36% of emigrants from the country were hired abroad, nearly double the corresponding percentage for immigrants to the country, which stood at 23%. Meanwhile, the job-search category was relatively similar for both immigrants and emigrants, accounting for 15% and 13% respectively. In contrast, the percentage of those immigrating for their studies was more than double that of emigrants, with their respective figures standing at 15% and 7%.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for the other reasons, exactly a quarter of immigrants went to this country to reunite with their families, compared to 15% of emigrants with the same purpose. Other, undisclosed reasons constituted significant proportions in both groups, accounting for 15% and 23% of migrants to and from this nation. Finally, only 7% and 4% of immigrants and emigrants relocated without any specific reason, making these percentages the smallest figures in the charts.
